correctness.rationale: Summing all displayed SIRS equations cancels progression and recovery to obtain z=N-S0 with z’=-mu*z-Σdelta_j I_j. Positivity and comparison give S-S0<=c exp(-mu t), c=(N0-S0)_+. I1’=[a1(R0-1)+beta(S-S0)] I1, so exponential decay if R0<1. At R0=1 a rescaling by exp[-beta*c*(1-e^-mu*t)/mu] is nonincreasing; hence I1 tends to finite L>=0. If L>0, strictly positive delta1 forces z eventually bounded below zero by a fixed amount, implying I1 declines exponentially, contradiction. Every downstream stage and R are exponentially stable scalar linear systems with vanishing input; N->S0, S->S0. Positive R0>1 eigenvalue gives instability. Checked algebra against source equations, including n=1, all nonnegative data and δ1>0; no claim of critical Lyapunov stability or endemic equilibrium.
